notes: NOT FROZEN until the freeze script writes judgments-manifest.json (this file is hashed then). Interpretation: the cross-category items are SUPPLEMENTARY GROSS-MISMATCH SANITY CHECKS. They are mostly easy negatives (unrelated subjects) and must not be presented as evidence of fine-grained visual discrimination. The near-miss items are provisional and are reported in two separate groups: ordinary near-misses (conditionType 'visual') and absence/negation cases (conditionType 'absence': NM02, NM04, NM06, NM08), which test whether a model handles 'empty' or 'no one' and must not be merged into a headline claim about ordinary scene relevance. Cross-category items reuse existing candidates (no extra downloads): the description of one scene is judged against the eight candidates of a scene from a different category. Near-miss items need 10 extra searches and up to 80 downloads (Stage C, not Stage A): the description names a specific visual condition and the query deliberately returns the opposite or unaffected condition. The reviewer decides in the blind sheet whether any candidate fits; a pair where the reviewer marks any candidate relevant is reported as contaminated and excluded from negative metrics, with the count disclosed.

crossCategory.rule: Within each split sort scene IDs ascending by sha256('xneg:'+id); the first 5 per split are description scenes. For description scene d the image scene is the scene in a DIFFERENT category with the lowest sha256('xneg-img:'+d+':'+m).
